spawn_allowlist.reason: BlockingExecutor owns a supervised async waiter for each admitted blocking job; this is the managed owner rather than an unowned caller spawn.
BlockingExecutor is the bounded capacity owner for unavoidable blocking work; production callers must enter through this executor instead of direct spawn_blocking.
ExitCoordinator owns the one async drain spawned from Tauri ExitRequested after preventing immediate exit.
OperationRegistry owns foreground operation join handles, cancellation and terminal events through this managed spawn.
TaskSupervisor owns scheduled task run handles and cancellation; permanent runner callers must register with it instead of spawning directly.

The Windows Explorer launcher is intentionally detached because Explorer can return a non-zero process status after successfully opening the directory; the helper starts no business work and owns no application state.
The proxy lifecycle writer owns a bounded channel worker for request/attempt finalization and is not a business-state bypass.

DualTerminalFinalizationLease owns a joinable request finalization task after reserving bounded lifecycle writer slots; response-body tests and production loopback prove the request terminal waits on attempt/cost acknowledgements instead of spawning unowned business work.
The proxy runtime facade owns the listener task and drains it through the public runtime lifecycle.
Startup auto-start schedules one owned proxy runtime start after setup without taking over request lifecycle.
The TaskSupervisor-owned Monitoring V2 runner keeps at most four worker futures in an owned JoinSet, applies station and key limits, and cancels plus drains the set during shutdown.
The capture command owns a short-lived, idempotent script reinjection sequence for the capture WebView after navigation; it does not own business work or persistence.
RuntimeLogService owns the bounded JSONL writer worker; event producers only try_send typed lines and shutdown flushes the owned worker.

http_client_construction_allowlist.reason: AsyncOutboundClient owns shared reqwest client construction and policy-keyed pooling for provider and management migrations.
Proxy request forwarding keeps its verified upstream client pool and lifecycle owner; Stage 4 only coordinates it through the runtime facade.
